transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith, I'm Maria. I go out of my way to avoid anything that reminds me of what happened to my cousin, even if it means cutting out parts of my life. My husband and my manager at work both noticed how much I've been pulling back lately, which is what finally pushed me to seek help.
Can you tell me more about the specific event involving your cousin, and how long ago it occurred?

About a year and a few months ago, my younger cousin was shot and killed during an armed robbery on a bus in Guatemala. I flew back there to help my family with the funeral, but being there, viewing his body, and hearing all the graphic details of the attack was just... devastating. It has been incredibly hard to move past it.
Have you experienced persistent symptoms like flashbacks, nightmares, or feeling 'on edge' continuously since the event, or have these symptoms only emerged or worsened in the last six months?

Yes, those symptoms have been happening steadily ever since I returned from Guatemala, which was a little over a year ago. I've been dealing with the vivid nightmares, sudden flashbacks of my cousin, and feeling constantly jumpy from the very beginning, rather than just starting in the last six months. It has been a constant struggle this whole time.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports persistent symptoms (flashbacks, nightmares, hyperarousal, and avoidance) lasting longer than six months since the index trauma. This duration and the presence of these core symptoms support the diagnosis of the chronic form of the disorder, ruling out the acute presentation (F43.11) and the delayed-onset presentation (F43.12).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following the witness of a traumatic event (death of a cousin via violence). She exhibits core symptoms including intrusion (nightmares, flashbacks), avoidance (avoiding reminders), and hyperarousal (feeling jumpy/on edge) persisting for over a year, causing functional impairment in her professional and personal life.
